perspective:
Jose Castillo’s available information:

- He works at the community bank as a heavy equipment operator/maintenance helper and knows Patricia Ndiaye as a bank teller/colleague with a friendly, professional relationship.
- He observed Patricia seeming more withdrawn/down than her usual vibrant self during shifts. He asked if she was okay. Patricia said it was “nothing really, just personal stuff,” thanked him, and appreciated his offer to listen.
- During a lunch break, he overheard Patricia on the phone sounding worried about bills and financial commitments.
- He offered to discuss financial planning strategies with her. Patricia said that could be helpful, that she had been overwhelmed with bills, and that she would take him up on it soon.
- He later worried he might have overstepped by bringing up finances. He told Patricia he hoped she didn’t mind and that he wasn’t prying. Patricia said she didn’t think he was prying, was grateful for the offer, and appreciated his support. He said he respected her privacy and wanted to support her as a friend; she said it was good to have someone to turn to.
- He asked how she was and about weekend plans. Patricia said she was all good and planned a quiet weekend at home. He shared his own plans and offered to be available if she needed anything. She thanked him and said she’d keep it in mind.
- He continued checking in at work and offering help, including grabbing coffee. Patricia said she was busy but handling it, thanked him for checking in, and said his support was great. He replied that he was there to help.
- He has his own impressions from these interactions, including sensing that Patricia appreciates his concern and may prefer to handle her issues privately. He does not know her full private financial or personal situation beyond what she explicitly said or what he overheard.
